use: X ga tokui = I'm good at X; fine to say about yourself without sounding like bragging.
notes: Opposite is nigate (weak at, not my thing). Jouzu is praise for others; tokui works for yourself.

use: X ga heta = bad at X; fine about yourself, blunt about others.

example.romaji: Uta, heta dakara karaoke wa iya.
example.ja: 歌、下手だからカラオケは嫌。
example.english: I'm bad at singing, so no karaoke.

examplePolite.romaji: Uta ga heta na node, karaoke wa chotto.
examplePolite.ja: 歌が下手なので、カラオケはちょっと。
examplePolite.english: I'm bad at singing, so karaoke isn't really for me.

notes: Opposite is jouzu. Nigate is 'not my thing'; heta is about lack of skill.

use: Praise for effort, even small: 'erai!' = well done!; 'erai hito' = a big shot.

example.romaji: Mainichi benkyou shiteru no? Erai ne!
example.ja: 毎日勉強してるの？偉いね！
example.english: You study every day? Good for you!

examplePolite.romaji: Mainichi benkyou shite iru n desu ka. Erai desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 毎日勉強しているんですか。偉いですね。
examplePolite.english: You study every day? That's impressive.

notes: Praising a superior with erai sounds condescending; use it for peers, juniors and kids.

use: Praise for someone who has grown up or done well, and for grand things like a big house.

example.romaji: Ano ko, rippa na otona ni natta ne.
example.ja: あの子、立派な大人になったね。
example.english: That kid grew up into a fine adult.

examplePolite.romaji: Ano ko wa rippa na otona ni narimashita ne.
examplePolite.ja: あの子は立派な大人になりましたね。
examplePolite.english: That child has grown into a fine adult.

notes: Rippa na ie = an impressive house. Sounds a little grown-up or formal from a young speaker.

use: Praise for ability at school or work; a bit formal.

example.romaji: Kanojo, sugoku yuushuu nan da yo.
example.ja: 彼女、すごく優秀なんだよ。

examplePolite.ja: 彼女はとても優秀です。

notes: About ability, not character; for character use rippa or erai.

use: -sa turns an adjective into a 'how much' noun: ookii (big) becomes ookisa (size).

example.ja: ちょうどいい大きさだね。

examplePolite.ja: ちょうどいい大きさですね。

notes: Saizu is for clothes and shop sizes; ookisa is how big anything is.

use: The shop word for S, M, L and shoe sizes.

example.ja: この靴、サイズが合わない。
example.english: These shoes are the wrong size.

examplePolite.romaji: Kono kutsu wa saizu ga aimasen.
examplePolite.ja: この靴はサイズが合いません。
examplePolite.english: These shoes are the wrong size.

notes: Usually with au (fit): saizu ga au / awanai.

use: Often just means how something looks: 'dezain ga kawaii' = it looks cute.

example.romaji: Kono kutsu, dezain ga ii ne.
example.ja: この靴、デザインがいいね。
example.english: I like the look of these shoes.

examplePolite.romaji: Kono kutsu wa dezain ga ii desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: この靴はデザインがいいですね。
examplePolite.english: These shoes have a nice design.

use: Goes after a number and includes it: 'sen'en ika' = 1,000 yen or less.

example.romaji: Sen'en ika no purezento ni shiyou.
example.ja: 千円以下のプレゼントにしよう。
example.english: Let's keep presents to 1,000 yen or less.

examplePolite.romaji: Sen'en ika no purezento ni shimashou.
examplePolite.ja: 千円以下のプレゼントにしましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's keep presents to 1,000 yen or less.

notes: Opposite is ijou (or more). Also 'the following' in announcements and writing.

use: A noun: 'okiniiri no mise' = my favourite shop; also the favourites button in apps.

example.romaji: Koko, watashi no okiniiri no kafe.
example.ja: ここ、私のお気に入りのカフェ。

examplePolite.romaji: Koko wa watashi no okiniiri no kafe desu.
examplePolite.ja: ここは私のお気に入りのカフェです。

notes: Ichiban suki (like best) is the everyday way to say which one is your favourite.

use: With a positive it means both; with a negative it means neither: 'dochira mo shiranai' = I don't know either.

example.ja: どちらもおいしそうだね。

examplePolite.ja: どちらもおいしそうですね。

notes: In casual talk it's usually dotchi mo.

use: Often a treat you give yourself: 'jibun e no gohoubi' = a little reward for me.

example.ja: 頑張ったから、自分にご褒美。
example.english: I worked hard, so I'm treating myself.

examplePolite.romaji: Ganbatta node, jibun ni gohoubi desu.
examplePolite.ja: 頑張ったので、自分にご褒美です。
examplePolite.english: I worked hard, so this is a treat for myself.

notes: Also for rewarding kids or pets.

example.english: Did you make a shopping list?

examplePolite.ja: 買い物リストは作りましたか？
examplePolite.english: Did you make the shopping list?

notes: Usually with tsukuru (make) or ni ireru (add to the list).

use: Mostly for kind acts, often by strangers: 'shinsetsu ni oshiete kureta' = kindly showed me.

example.romaji: Michi o kiitara, shinsetsu ni oshiete kureta.
example.ja: 道を聞いたら、親切に教えてくれた。
example.english: I asked for directions and they kindly showed me.

examplePolite.romaji: Michi o kiitara, shinsetsu ni oshiete kuremashita.
examplePolite.ja: 道を聞いたら、親切に教えてくれました。
examplePolite.english: I asked for directions and they kindly showed me.

notes: Yasashii is kind as a personality; shinsetsu is kind in what someone does.

use: Short for naka ga ii; describes a relationship, not one person.

example.romaji: Ano futari, honto ni naka ii yo ne.
example.ja: あの二人、ほんとに仲いいよね。
example.english: Those two really get along, don't they?

examplePolite.romaji: Ano futari wa hontou ni naka ga ii desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: あの二人は本当に仲がいいですね。
examplePolite.english: Those two really get along, don't they?

notes: Opposite: naka ga warui. Nakayoku shite = play nicely (to kids).

english: reliable; someone you can count on
use: Praise for a person you can lean on: 'tayori ni naru senpai' = a senior I can count on.

example.romaji: Ane wa itsumo tayori ni naru n da.
example.ja: 姉はいつも頼りになるんだ。
example.english: I can always count on my big sister.

examplePolite.romaji: Ane wa itsumo tayori ni narimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 姉はいつも頼りになります。
examplePolite.english: I can always count on my older sister.

notes: Opposite: tayorinai (unreliable). Tayoru = to rely on.

use: Describes how close people are: 'shitashii tomodachi' = a close friend.

example.romaji: Kare to wa sonna ni shitashikunai yo.
example.ja: 彼とはそんなに親しくないよ。
example.english: I'm not that close with him.

examplePolite.romaji: Kare to wa sonna ni shitashikunai desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼とはそんなに親しくないです。
examplePolite.english: I'm not that close with him.

notes: In speech naka ga ii is more common; shitashii sounds slightly more careful.
